title: Python SDK: multiplex stream adapter and deterministic replay cookbook
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Implement a multiplexing adapter in the Python SDK that lets a single streaming connection deliver typed events to multiple logical consumers, plus a deterministic replay mode for unit/integration tests and CI. Improve backpressure signals and provide cookbook examples for common developer patterns.
description:
Problem: Users want ergonomic patterns for consuming streamed chat completions and sideband events (tool calls, structured deltas, partial function args) without shipping brittle ad-hoc parsing in each app. Two common pain points are (1) developers needing to demux a single SSE/WebSocket stream into multiple handlers while preserving ordering and idempotency, and (2) tests that are flaky because stream timing affects assertions.

Goal: Add a first-class MultiplexStreamAdapter in the Python SDK with explicit event typing, lightweight subscription API, and checkpointable consumer cursors. Add a deterministic replay harness (replay mode) that can record streams in CI or local dev and deterministically replay them for unit tests and golden evaluation. Provide cookbook docs and 3 canonical examples: fan-out to analytics+UI, resumable request processing with idempotent sinks, and deterministic regression tests for prompt/eval changes.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change the underlying server protocol or implement new wire-level guarantees beyond documenting expected ordering; it focuses on client-side ergonomics and test tooling.
acceptance_criteria: MultiplexStreamAdapter is available in sdk.python.streams with a small subscription API (subscribe(event_type, callback_or_async_iterator))
Adapter supports sync and async consumers and preserves event order per conversation id
Adapter exposes backpressure signals (paused/resumed) and a configurable buffer limit with documented default behavior
Checkpoint API: consumers can create/save/load lightweight cursors so resumed consumers start from last-acknowledged event
Replay harness: record() and replay(file) utilities exist and replay deterministically in tests without requiring network
Three cookbook examples added to docs: analytics+ui fanout, resumable sink with exactly-once semantics, deterministic eval test
Unit tests covering adapter subscribe/unsubscribe, buffer overflow behavior, checkpoint semantics, and replay correctness
API reviewed by SDK and Platform owners and a small benchmark shows <5% overhead in median latency for streaming path with adapter enabled
implementation_notes: Design an event envelope shape: {event_type, conversation_id, seq, timestamp, payload} (documented schema in design doc)
MultiplexStreamAdapter maintains per-conversation sequence monotonically increasing; global ordering not required but per-conversation ordering enforced
Backpressure: adapter exposes an async wait_for_resume() for consumers; default buffer limit 1024 events, configurable via adapter config

Replay mode: record writes newline-delimited JSONL with exact envelopes; replay reads and injects into adapter event loop with recorded deltas between timestamps or in 'tight' mode for fastest execution
Provide both a lightweight sync façade for quick scripts and an async-first surface for production code
Telemetry: emit metrics for buffer_fill, resume_count, replay_mode_active for Console dashboard linking
Do a short mem/latency profile comparing direct consumer vs adapter on a synthetic workload (5k small events/sec)
steps: Write design doc and get alignment with SDK and Platform teams
Implement adapter skeleton with subscribe/unsubscribe and event dispatch loop
Add per-conversation seq enforcement and simple in-memory cursor store
Add replay recorder and replay runner utilities
Write cookbook examples and docs, add unit/integration tests
Run benchmarks and iterate on buffer sizing and wakeup logic
API review and merge, then backport docs to examples repository
testing_plan: Unit tests: subscribe/unsubscribe, ordering guarantees, cursor save/load, overflow behavior
Integration tests: adapter with live staging stream (smoke), ensure telemetry emitted
Replay tests: record a failing flakey test in CI, assert deterministic replay yields same events and pass/fail state
Load test: synthetic producer @5k events/sec for 60s, measure P50/P99 latency increase and memory usage
Fuzz: malformed envelopes and missing seq handling
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Adapter buffer growth causes OOM under bursty workloads; Mitigation: default bounded buffer with drop policy and consumer backoff signals
Risk: Replay recorded files leak PII; Mitigation: replay recorder supports a redaction hook and recommend storing in secured artifact storage
Risk: Consumers make blocking sync calls and stall event loop; Mitigation: provide guidance and helper run_in_executor wrapper and documented best practices
Risk: Incorrect seq handling with mixed sync/async consumers; Mitigation: enforce ordering at adapter boundary and test mixed consumer permutations
notes: Early prototype exists in branch feature/multiplex-adapter-proto with basic API; experiment showed 3% median latency overhead on microbenchmarks
We should consider a small public sample demonstrating how to convert an existing SSE-based consumer to the adapter in <20 LOC
Follow-up ticket will add Redis-backed durable cursor store for Dedicated/Private deployments (not in scope for this ticket)
